To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the binding of Ru(bpy)(3) to DNA is cooperative and anticooperative, whereas the binding of Ru(2+) to the dendrims is noncooperative and cooperative.
the binding of a ruthenium complex with DNA is anticooperative and the addition of an electrolyte changes the cooperative nature of this process.
the cooperative binding of the * Ru(bpy)(3) complex to DNA is related to the ionic strength and the presence of a salt in the reaction medium.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of the ionic strength on the binding of a complex to a macromolecular receptor.
the study of the binding of a *Ru(bpy(3))(2+) complex to the SB4. 5G dendriner and to DNA.
the cooperative and noncooperative character of the ligand-receptor binding, as well as with the influence of the ionic strength on the binding process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cooperative binding is a consequence of a strong binding of the complex in the first step of the reaction, followed by a second step in which the binding is weak.

the cooperative character of a binding reaction depends on the nature of the ligands, the receptor, and the reaction medium. , in the presence of an electrolyte, the binding to the DNA is noncooperative, whereas in its absence, the binding shows a negative cooperativeness.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the binding of *Ru(2+) to the DNA and SB4,5G dendrimer is cooperative in nature.
the SB4. 5G dendrizers are a good model for DNA in the study of the cooperative character of the binding of *Ru (bpy)(3)(3+) complex.
the binding of *Ru(2+) to both DNA and the dendrimer can be explained in terms of a competition between electrostatic interactions, which are the main attractive force, and the entropy of the system.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the cooperative and noncooperative character of the ligand/DNA binding is a function of the ionic strength and that the ionic nature of the ligands is a crucial parameter to consider in the study of ligand/DNA interactions.
the binding of *Ru (bpy)(3)(+2) complex to DNA shows anticooperative character, while the binding to the SB4. 5G dendriner is noncooperative.
the ionic character of the ligand and receptor plays a crucial role on the binding process, which is not the case for neutral ligands and receptors.
